title: Diabetes incidence in South Asians across weight categories: BMJ Open Diabetes Research & Care 2021
authors: Narayan KMV, Gujral UP, Mohan V, et al.
study_type: Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study (Chennai, Delhi, Karachi)
primary_intervention: Epidemiological incidence tracking across normal BMI (<25 kg/m2) vs overweight

key_findings.claim: South Asian men with normal BMI (<25 kg/m2) have 2.9 times higher diabetes incidence adjusted for age compared to white counterparts.
key_findings.citation_location: BMJ Open Diabetes Res Care 2021;9:e001997 (PMC8006839), p4-s12
key_findings.clinical_interpretation: Normal BMI fails to detect catastrophic metabolic risk in lean Indian men.

key_findings.claim: South Asian women with normal BMI (<25 kg/m2) have 5.3 times higher diabetes incidence adjusted for age compared to white women.
key_findings.citation_location: BMJ Open Diabetes Res Care 2021;9:e001997 (PMC8006839), p4-s13
key_findings.clinical_interpretation: Lean Indian women suffer a 5.3-fold elevated risk due to hidden visceral ectopic fat.

key_findings.claim: Metabolic decompensation and ectopic visceral adiposity in South Asians triggers at BMI 22 kg/m2, well below the Western 25 kg/m2 threshold.
key_findings.citation_location: BMJ Open Diabetes Res Care 2021;9:e001997 (PMC8006839), p6-s21
key_findings.clinical_interpretation: DEXA visceral fat scanning and fasting insulin biomarkers must replace the weighing scale.

adverse_events: Epidemiological study; severe cardiometabolic risk occurs prematurely in lean South Asian adults.
clinical_implication: Proves the weighing scale is an obsolete diagnostic for Indian bodies. DEXA visceral fat imaging and fasting insulin biomarkers must replace BMI to diagnose the thin-fat TOFI phenotype.
